title: Price of Smoothness Adaptation in Causal Distribution-Energy Testing
banked_reason: Independent validity gate: sound-below-floor, not laundering. Math passes and citations are verified; the committed full-B sharp frontier remains openly unresolved. Delivered matched honest n^-3/11 benchmark and unmatched full-B upper bound are incremental; no bounded repair reaches field.
gap_reasons: The committed evaluable full-(gamma,s,beta) beta-blind common inflation and its attaining test remain explicitly to-prove; the proved single-smoothness honest benchmark and loose upper bounds are a weaker substituted object, not the promised Stat decision deliverable.
The promised nuisance-dependent comparison with the revealed-propensity adaptation price has no explicit full-region ratio or transition map: this node retains it as open and supplies only brackets.
proof_attempt_summary: Attempted the full unknown-smoothness causal energy adaptation frontier at field novelty. Discovery derived and independently audited a matched union-null honest n^-3/11 benchmark at (gamma,s,beta)=(1/16,3/16,1/3), source-verified its cited leaves, and obtained an unmatched full-B upper Lambda_n <= C n^7/55. The beta-aware normalization, exact common inflation, and full-region transitions remain open; no Lean formalization was launched, and retry requires genuinely new matching proofs rather than reframing or an identical resume.
tldr: The sharp adaptation price for marginal causal distribution-energy testing remains the central open question. A matched honest benchmark is now proved: at \((\gamma,s)=(1/16,3/16)\), one observable beta-blind test has size at most \(0.05\) on the entire marginal-null union and worst miss at most \(0.2\) at energy \(C n^{-3/11}\) for every member with outcome smoothness \(1/3\); an all-test converse matches that order. This implies \(\Lambda_n r_n(1/3)\ge c n^{-3/11}\), but does not establish the proposed common factor \(n^{5/627}\). The revealed-propensity price is matched, a stronger conservative full-interval common upper factor \(C n^{7/55}\) is attained at the unequal benchmark, and an iterated-logarithmic lower price persists when \(\gamma+s>2/5\). The exact whole-square, full-interval common inflation and its transition factors remain unresolved.
gap: Ordinary adaptive two-sample theory addresses directly observed densities. Fixed-kernel causal testing adjusts for confounding but does not characterize sharp simultaneous global \(L^2\) sensitivity over unknown outcome smoothness. The conditional rough-null class changes with \(\beta\), which creates a distinct honesty comparison.
fill: Derive \(R_n\) and \(L_n\) from matching fixed-sample likelihood and observable contraction bounds, with all-test lower bounds and one finite-data level-\(0.05\) beta-blind detector. Resolve the reversed asymmetry and all slow factors, rather than declaring nuisance dominance to erase adaptation.
